content:
Apple Music seems to be rolling out a new logo, which has been spotted in several places, including iOS 27 beta 3.

The new Apple Music logo features a bolder typeface and an all-lowercase design.

Last month, when Apple announced the opening of Apple Music Hall, it displayed a never-before-seen new logo.

You can see the new logo on the official Apple Music Hall website, with a light version at the top of the page and a dark version at the bottom.

At the time, it was unclear whether the logo was only for that venue's branding, as its bold typeface matched the overall style of Apple Music Hall.

However, since then, Apple has already used the new logo in some Instagram Reels unrelated to Apple Music Hall. And today, Aaron Perris found related evidence in iOS 27.2 beta 3.

The most-liked comment was posted by CyanLobster.

Ah, this is the dilemma of app icon design:

Users get tired of the existing icon, but don't like it when the icon changes.

The official Apple Music website still uses the old design, but based on Apple's process of gradually renaming Apple TV+ to Apple TV last year, Apple is never in a rush when it comes to brand updates.

Rebranding is a bigger project than changing a logo, but it's understandable that Apple would roll out the redesigned Apple Music logo gradually in a similar manner.

What do you think of the new Apple Music logo? Let us know in the comments.

Apple Music costs $11.99 per month, and is also available as part of the Apple One bundle.
